title: Zariski's main theorem at a quasi-finite prime: a finite subalgebra agreeing with S away from g
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a ring map such that $S$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra, let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime ideal, and assume that $R\to S$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. Then there are an $R$-subalgebra $S'\subseteq S$ which is a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and an element $g\in S'$ with $g\notin\mathfrak q$ such that the ring map $S'_g\to S_g$, $y/g^n\mapsto y/g^n$, between the localizations of $S'$ and of $S$ at the powers of $g$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], induced by the inclusion $S'\subseteq S$, is an isomorphism.

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 00Q9 (theorem-main-theorem, line 30779: $g\in S'$ integral closure, $g\notin\mathfrak q$, $S'_g\cong S_g$) together with the construction of the finite subalgebra in the proof of Lemma Tag 00QB (3) (lemma-quasi-finite-open-integral-closure, line 30906: the sub-$R$-algebra generated by $g$ and elements $y_j$ of $S'$ whose fractions generate $S'_g$; 'details omitted'); this is the form used at the start of the proof of Lemma Tag 07NC (line 31064). Stacks 00QB assumes $S$ quasi-finite over $R$ at every prime; the pointwise form here needs only 00Q9. Tags verified in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags (00Q9, 00QB, 07NC).

proof.text: *Zariski's main theorem.* Let $S'\subseteq S$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $S$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], an $R$-subalgebra of $S$. The hypothesis that $R\to S$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime] is Stacks' Definition 00PL (taken with condition (1) of Lemma 00PK), which is the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-zariski-main-away] (stated there as 'quasi-finite in the affine sense, Stacks Algebra Definition 10.122.3, Tags 00PL and 00PK'); $S$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-zariski-main-away] with $A=R$, $B=S$, $B'=S'$ gives $g\in S'$ with $g\notin\mathfrak q$ such that the map $S'_g\to S_g$, $y/g^n\mapsto y/g^n$, of localizations at the powers of $g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] induced by the inclusion $S'\subseteq S$ is an isomorphism; in particular it is surjective.

*Choice of numerators.* Choose $s_1,\dots,s_m\in S$ generating $S$ as an $R$-algebra. By the surjectivity of $S'_g\to S_g$ (step 1), for each $i$ there are $y_i\in S'$ and $n_i\ge0$ with $y_i/g^{n_i}=s_i/1$ in $S_g$; by the definition of equality in $S_g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] this means $g^{k_i}(y_i-g^{n_i}s_i)=0$ in $S$ for some $k_i\ge0$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00QA (lemma-quasi-finite-open), lines 30886-30893 (S'' the sub-R-algebra of S' generated by g, y_1,...,y_N, finite over R by Lemma Tag 00GM), the same construction as in the proof of Lemma Tag 00QB (3), line 30944 ('Details omitted')

proof.text: *The finite subalgebra.* Let $S''\subseteq S$ be the $R$-subalgebra generated by $g,y_1,\dots,y_m$. Since $S'$ is an $R$-subalgebra containing these elements, $S''\subseteq S'$, so each generator of $S''$ is integral over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]: a monic relation $x^d+\varphi(r_{d-1})x^{d-1}+\dots+\varphi(r_0)=0$ holding in $S$ holds in the subring $S''$, which contains $\varphi(R)$. Hence $S''$ is an $R$-algebra generated by finitely many elements integral over $R$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-of-integral-generators] it is a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Moreover $g\in S''$ and $g\notin\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00QA (lemma-quasi-finite-open), lines 30886-30893 (S'' the sub-R-algebra of S' generated by g, y_1,...,y_N, finite over R by Lemma Tag 00GM), the same construction as in the proof of Lemma Tag 00QB (3), line 30944 ('Details omitted'); finiteness: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00GM (lemma-characterize-integral), in the DAG Lemma Tag 02JJ (3)=>(1)

proof.text: *Injectivity of $S''_g\to S_g$.* Let $\iota:S''_g\to S_g$, $y/g^n\mapsto y/g^n$, be the ring map induced by the inclusion $S''\subseteq S$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], [def-weil-ring-localization-away] (well defined: an equation $g^k(g^{n'}y-g^ny')=0$ in $S''$ holds in $S$). If $\iota(y/g^n)=0$, then $y/1=0$ in $S_g$, so $g^ky=0$ in $S$ for some $k\ge0$; since $S''$ is a subring of $S$ containing $g$ and $y$, the same equation $g^ky=0$ holds in $S''$, hence $y/g^n=0$ in $S''_g$. So the kernel of $\iota$ is zero and $\iota$ is injective.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00QA (lemma-quasi-finite-open), lines 30886-30893 (S'' the sub-R-algebra of S' generated by g, y_1,...,y_N, finite over R by Lemma Tag 00GM), the same construction as in the proof of Lemma Tag 00QB (3), line 30944 ('Details omitted') (the details omitted there)

proof.text: *Surjectivity of $S''_g\to S_g$, and conclusion.* The image of $\iota$ is an $R$-subalgebra of $S_g$. It contains $1/g=\iota(1/g)$ (as $g\in S''$) and, for each $i$, $s_i/1=y_i/g^{n_i}=\iota(y_i/g^{n_i})$ (step 2, as $y_i\in S''$). Every element of $S_g$ has the form $s/g^n$ with $s\in S$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], and $s=P(s_1,\dots,s_m)$ for a polynomial $P$ with coefficients in $R$, so $s/g^n=P(s_1/1,\dots,s_m/1)\cdot(1/g)^n$ lies in the image of $\iota$. Hence $\iota$ is surjective, and with step 4 a ring isomorphism $S''_g\cong S_g$. By step 3, $S''$ (in the role of the statement's $S'$) is an $R$-subalgebra of $S$ which is a finitely generated $R$-module, with $g\in S''$, $g\notin\mathfrak q$, and $S''_g\to S_g$ an isomorphism.
